props.title: Running Out of Time
props.initialSlug: Cop races against time to outsmart dying mastermind

sections.content: **Running Out of Time** (1999) revolutionized Hong Kong action thrillers through Johnnie To's masterful direction and Andy Lau's electric performance. The film follows a terminally ill criminal mastermind playing a complex cat-and-mouse game with a negotiator over 72 hours. It shares DNA with Michael Mann's **Heat** (1995) in its cerebral approach to crime and psychological warfare, while anticipating the intricate plotting of **Inside Man** (2006). To's signature style - mixing tense standoffs with philosophical undertones - influenced later Hong Kong cinema like **Infernal Affairs** (2002).

sections.content: The film established Johnnie To as Hong Kong's premier crime stylist, paving the way for his later masterpieces like **Election** (2005) and **Drug War** (2012). To's meticulous attention to urban geography and preference for subtle character moments over action spectacle created a new template for Asian crime cinema. The influence can be seen in Korean thrillers like **The Chaser** (2008) and **The Yellow Sea** (2010), which similarly emphasize psychological warfare over gunplay.

Andy Lau's portrayal of the dying criminal mastermind Cheung echoes through later performances like Tony Leung in **Infernal Affairs** (2002) and Aaron Kwok in **Port of Call** (2015). The theme of limited time driving criminal schemes would later appear in films like **Crippled Avengers** (2009) and **Life Without Principle** (2011), though none matched Running Out of Time's perfect balance of action and existential drama. sections.content: The film's influence extends beyond Asia. Christopher Nolan cited it as inspiration for **The Dark Knight** (2008)'s elaborate criminal schemes. The "mastermind criminal surrendering as part of the plan" trope popularized here echoes through **Inside Man** (2006), **Skyfall** (2012), and **Prison Break** (2005). To's use of Hong Kong's verticality and urban canyons influenced how directors like Michael Mann shot cities in films like **Miami Vice** (2006) and **Blackhat** (2015).
